authoritative_for: Bazaar owns exact opaque string content and append-only per-ID versions, its local read/write API, database initialization, and program installation.
not_authoritative_for: Callers own identifier meaning, content formats, prompt roles, templates, model configuration interpretation, agent invocation, and domain success.

covers: All public string reads, version-history reads, appends, initialization, integrity checks, and program installation/recovery outcomes.
excludes: Help/version, implementation helpers, templating, content interpretation, model execution, caller migration, and arbitrary direct SQL access.

shared_access_and_trust: The current user owns private local state. The Rust API operates in process. Agent readers have read-only database access; explicit writers append. No daemon, network listener, or application-level authentication is supplied.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Content and IDs may be sensitive. Every committed version is retained without automatic deletion. CLI command usage recording omits arguments and content and preserves results after recording errors.
compatibility_and_retirement: String versions, database schema one, output schema one, capability versions and product releases are independent. Unsupported or foreign state fails without automatic migration.
operational_limits: Each update changes one ID. Reads of different IDs have separate snapshots. The service stores whole strings and returns whole version-number histories; no capacity, throughput or latency guarantee is supplied.
